reported_frozen_findings.title: Keep collection numerators in campaign units before one normalization
reported_frozen_findings.reason: Collection methods label a quantity the recorded numerator yet define it as consumed material/accepted kg, purchased kWh×3.6/accepted kg, or emission kg/accepted kg. Declared unit is kg or MJ. Cards then say collect the amount through that protocol and divide by accepted kg; line308 and normalize_batch314 require all raw numerators to be campaign totals and divide once. These are inconsistent local instructions.
reported_frozen_findings.consequence: A reader obeying the collection numerator formula and the later card formula divides twice, or stores MJ/kg in a field labelled MJ. The later once-only paragraph exposes intended behavior but does not repair the contradictory numerator definition.

counterexample.interpretation: Dimensional and arithmetic demonstration of conflicting instructions only; no claimed factory observations.

reported_frozen_findings.requested_correction: Collect unnormalized native material kg, kWh or converted MJ and emitted kg in protocols; identify normalization as one shared reporting operation, not a numerator. Preserve same B and any final reporting formulas without adding a second division.
reported_frozen_findings.limits: Actual implementation may correctly follow the once-only paragraph; finding concerns misleading and dimensionally inconsistent author-facing instructions.

reported_frozen_findings.title: Use demand V_provider in every chip and gas card after separating fixed provider reference
reported_frozen_findings.reason: The complete measurement rule, cp_feed and calculations reserve fixed A_provider for provider reference and V_provider for converted period demand, but chip quantity conditions/cards still say convert to A and use reference volume A per1kg; gas card similarly uses reference volume A. The old A notation and new explicit fixed reference are left inconsistent in the same quantity contract.
reported_frozen_findings.consequence: A consumer can use a fixed1m3 provider reference as the demanded quantity even when actual period demand is10m3. The explicit calc rule is correct, so the defect is an incomplete symbol migration in card instructions, not the underlying state-conversion algebra.
reported_frozen_findings.requested_correction: Reserve A_provider for fixed provider reference; update every chip/gas preamble, card amount and cp_fuel/reference phrase to converted period V_provider, exchangeV_provider/Q and separate n_provider=V_provider/A_provider. Regenerate projection and keep state/definition gaps.
reported_frozen_findings.limits: A may have been intended as shorthand for demand in old cards. The new rule removes that meaning, so this is a confirmed cross-field ambiguity; no measured downstream wrong quantity is claimed.
